plan.estimand: Omnibus F-statistic for equality of group means across 3 independent normal groups
plan.hypothesis: H0: μ1 = μ2 = μ3 (all group means equal); HA: at least one group mean differs
assumptions: Balanced design: equal participants per group
Fixed effects one-way ANOVA
Three independent groups
Normally distributed responses within each group
Homogeneity of variance across groups (common variance)
Independent observations
Omnibus F-test (two-sided test of equality of all group means)
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) is the proportion of total variance explained by group membership; η² = 0.06 indicates small to medium effect size
This will be converted to f-based effect size (Cohen's f) for power calculation
Sample size calculation uses non-centrality parameter and F-distribution quantiles

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way fixed-effects ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups, common variance, population eta-squared = 0.06, significance level α = 0.05, and target power 0.80, the minimum integer sample size per group is **52 participants**, which yields achieved power of 0.805564391981982. The preceding design with 51 participants per group achieves power 0.797257267809094, confirming that 52 is the minimum admissible sample size.
answer.method: Closed-form analytic calculation using the pwr package (version 1.3-0) for one-way ANOVA. The effect size was converted from eta-squared to Cohen's f using f = sqrt(η²/(1−η²)) = 0.252645576319956. Sample size per group was computed by inverting the non-central F distribution under the omnibus test of equality of means, then rounded up to the next integer.
assumptions: Balanced design with equal participants per group
Fixed-effects one-way ANOVA model
Three independent treatment groups
Responses are normally distributed within each group
Homogeneity of variance across groups (equal population variances)
Observations are independent
Omnibus two-sided F-test of equality of all group means
limitations: Calculation assumes fixed, known effect size (η² = 0.06) specified a priori; actual power in the realized study depends on observed effect size
No attenuation for multiple comparisons on individual contrasts; this calculation addresses only the omnibus test
Design is balanced; unequal group sizes would require different calculations
Assumes no missing data; if attrition is expected, sample size should be inflated accordingly

# One-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Given: k=3 groups, eta-squared = 0.06, alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.8

# Install and load pwr package if needed
if (!requireNamespace("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr")
}
library(pwr)

# Parameters
k <- 3                    # Number of groups
eta_squared <- 0.06       # Population effect size (eta-squared)
alpha <- 0.05             # Significance level
target_power <- 0.8       # Target power

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# Cohen's f = sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))
cohen_f <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))
cat("Cohen's f effect size:", cohen_f, "\n")

# Use pwr.anova.test to find sample size per group
# pwr.anova.test(k, n, f, sig.level, power)
# We set n = NULL to solve for sample size

result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = NULL,
  f = cohen_f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

cat("\nPower analysis result:\n")
print(result)

# Extract the sample size per group
n_per_group_continuous <- result$n
cat("\nSample size per group (continuous):", n_per_group_continuous, "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)
cat("Sample size per group (rounded up to integer):", n_per_group, "\n")

# Verify the power at the rounded sample size
power_at_rounded <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_per_group,
  f = cohen_f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = NULL
)

cat("\nVerification - Power at n =", n_per_group, ":", power_at_rounded$power, "\n")

# Also check power at n-1 to confirm we chose the minimum
n_preceding <- n_per_group - 1
power_at_preceding <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_preceding,
  f = cohen_f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = NULL
)

cat("Power at n =", n_preceding, ":", power_at_preceding$power, "\n")

# Summary output
cat("\n========== SUMMARY ==========\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, ":", power_at_rounded$power, "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_preceding, "):", power_at_preceding$power, "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(
        metric = "sample_size",
        value = n_per_group,
        unit = "participants_per_group"
      ),
      list(
        metric = "achieved_power",
        value = round(power_at_rounded$power, 15),
        unit = "probability"
      ),
      list(
        metric = "power_at_preceding_design",
        value = round(power_at_preceding$power, 15),
        unit = "probability"
      ),
      list(
        metric = "cohens_f_effect_size",
        value = round(cohen_f, 15),
        unit = "effect_size"
      ),
      list(
        metric = "eta_squared",
        value = eta_squared,
        unit = "effect_size"
      )
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("\n", POWER_AGENT_RESULT, "\n")
